label: input token t in the original phase (position >= 2)
explanation: Fires exactly when the letter t is input during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at position 2 or later; dev P=R=F1=1.0. Magnitude is weak at position 2 (~0.1-0.15 of max, only ~4% of mass) and strong (~0.6-1.0 of max) from position 3 onward; repeated t within a sequence still fires. Does not fire on t at positions 0-1, on any other token, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (including when t is fed back as an output). No dependence on L, first token, or neighbouring tokens beyond position.

issues: No refutation found. On the test split the predicate scores precision 1.0, recall 1.0 and F1 1.0 (mass recall about 1.0, n_active = n_predicted = 74555), and misses lists 0 missed activations and 0 false positives.

Each claim in the profile checks out. Activation is 0 in the delimiter and copy phases. It is 0 at t = 0 and 1. At t = 2 it carries 4.2% of the activation mass, and the lowest-quartile examples sit around 0.09-0.14 of max. Top examples at t >= 3 are about 0.6-1.0 of max. Repeated t's fire (for example 't t' at about 0.98 and 0.95). The firing rate within orig_idx >= 2 is a flat 0.033-0.034, so it does not depend on L. Breakdowns by first_tok, prev_tok and prev2_tok are flat.

Minor point, not a refutation: the explanation says it does not depend on L or neighbouring tokens, which is true of the firing rate. I did not check finer magnitude variation within t >= 3 in detail.
